questions.question:
Given `

Hi

` and the rules `p { color: green; }`, `.text { color: blue; }`, `#intro { color: red; }`, what colour is the text?
questions.explication: Specificity decides between matching rules: ID selector (#intro) beats class (.text), which beats type (p). So red wins.
questions.piege: Source order ("last rule wins") only matters when the competing rules have the SAME specificity.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the CSS specificity order from highest to lowest?
questions.explication: Inline styles are the most specific, then ID selectors, then class selectors, then type (tag) selectors.

questions.question: What is a callback function in JavaScript?
choix: A function declared as a method inside an object
A function that runs automatically on page load
A function that keeps calling itself until a condition is met
A function passed as an argument to another function
questions.explication: A callback is passed as an argument (e.g. `sayHello("Alice", farewell)`) and called later by the receiving function.

questions.question:
What does this code print?
`function sayHello(name, cb) { console.log("Hello, " + name); cb(); }`
`function farewell() { console.log("Goodbye!"); }`
`sayHello("Alice", farewell);`
choix: A TypeError: cb is not defined
questions.explication: sayHello first logs the greeting, then calls the callback `cb()`, which is `farewell`.
questions.piege: Passing `farewell` (no parentheses) passes the function itself; `farewell()` would call it immediately.

questions.question: In the CSS box model, what is the order of layers from the inside out?
questions.explication: Content sits in the middle, padding surrounds it, then the border, and margin is the outer space.
questions.piege: Padding is INSIDE the border, margin is OUTSIDE it.

questions.question: Which line correctly links an external stylesheet?
questions.explication: External CSS uses `<link rel="stylesheet" href="...">`. External JS uses `<script src="...">`.

questions.question:
This handler never runs. Why?
`document.getElementById("myBtn").addEventListener("onclick", function() { alert("Hi"); });`
choix: The callback must be a named function, not anonymous
addEventListener only works on links, not buttons
The event name must be "click", not "onclick"
getElementById needs a "#" before the id value
questions.explication: addEventListener takes the event name without the "on" prefix: "click", "mouseover", "keydown", "submit". The "on" prefix is for HTML attributes like `onclick="..."`.
questions.piege: `getElementById("myBtn")` takes the bare id. The "#" is only used in CSS selectors / querySelector.

questions.question: Which of these is an element PROPERTY (rather than an HTML attribute) according to the course?
questions.explication: Attributes (class, id, src, href) are written in the markup. Properties such as innerHTML and value are characteristics accessed through JavaScript.

questions.question:
What is printed?
`console.log('First');`
`setTimeout(() => console.log('Second'), 2000);`
`console.log('Third');`
questions.explication: setTimeout is asynchronous: it schedules 'Second' and lets the next line run right away, so 'Third' prints before 'Second'.

questions.question: What is a Single-Page Application (SPA)?
choix: An app made of a single component with no routing at all
An app where every link reloads a brand-new HTML page from the server
An app that loads one HTML page and updates content dynamically
An app whose pages are all generated by Pug on the server
questions.explication: An SPA loads a single HTML page once, then JavaScript swaps views without full page reloads.

questions.question: In an SPA built with Vue.js, who handles routing when the user clicks a link?
choix: The web server, which sends a new HTML file
The database, which picks the matching view
The DNS server, which resolves the new path
questions.explication: In SPAs routing is client-side: Vue Router reads the new URL and displays the matching component without reloading the page.
questions.piege: Full page reloads per URL are typical of traditional multi-page applications (MPA).

questions.question: What does React use to render efficiently and avoid re-rendering the entire UI?
questions.explication: React compares a Virtual DOM with the previous one and only updates what changed. Two-way binding and dependency injection are Angular features.

questions.question: Which example illustrates DECLARATIVE programming, as described in the course?
questions.explication: Declarative code describes WHAT you want (SQL query, HTML structure), not HOW to do it step by step. Components also follow this style.

questions.question: In the MVC example with Vue.js, which part is the `updateMessage` method that changes `message` when a button is clicked?
questions.explication:
Model = the `message` data, View = `

{{ message }}

`, Controller = the method that reacts to user input and modifies the model.

questions.question: What is the main difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
choix: HTTPS sends pages without any headers
HTTPS only works with the POST request method
HTTPS skips the DNS lookup entirely
questions.explication: HTTPS is HTTP with authentication and encryption (SSL/TLS certificate). HTTP sends data unencrypted.

questions.question: Which statement about the POST method is TRUE?
choix: Data is sent in the request body
Data appears in the URL query string
The request is cached by the browser
questions.explication: POST puts data in the body, is not cached, does not appear in history, cannot be bookmarked and has no length limit. The other three options describe GET.
questions.piege: Use GET to retrieve data; use POST to create/update data or to send sensitive data.

questions.question: In a Vue instance, what is the role of the `el` option?
choix: It mounts Vue to a DOM element
questions.explication: el = mounting point (e.g. '#app'); data = reactive data; computed = derived state; methods = functions/behaviour.

questions.question: Which option should hold a value derived from other data, e.g. a reversed message?
questions.explication: computed defines reactive, derived state: `reversedMessage()` is recalculated automatically when `message` changes.

questions.question: With `message: 'Hello, Vue!'`, what does `{{ reversedMessage }}` display, given `reversedMessage() { return this.message.split('').reverse().join(''); }`?
questions.explication: split('') makes an array of characters, reverse() reverses it, join('') rebuilds the string: every character, including the comma and space, is reversed.

questions.question: In Vue 2, how do you make a property added dynamically after creation reactive?
questions.explication: Vue 2 (Object.defineProperty) cannot detect new properties, so `Vue.set(this.$data, 'prop', value)` is needed. In Vue 3, `reactive()` (Proxy) handles new properties automatically.
questions.piege: `reactive()` is the Vue 3 answer, not Vue 2.

questions.question: Which mechanism does Vue 3 use behind the scenes to track data changes?
questions.explication: Vue 2 uses getters/setters via Object.defineProperty; Vue 3 uses Proxy, which also detects added properties.

questions.question: Which code correctly creates and mounts a Vue 3 application?
questions.explication: Vue 3: `const { createApp } = Vue; createApp({...}).mount('#app')`. Vue 2 used `new Vue({ el: '#app', ... })` or `.$mount('#app')`.

questions.question:
With `html: 'Hi'`, what does `

` display?
choix: Nothing, because v-text strips HTML tags
The word Hi rendered in bold type
questions.explication: v-text renders plain text, so tags are shown as text. To interpret the HTML you need v-html.
questions.piege: v-html renders raw HTML; v-text and {{ }} do not.

questions.question: Which directive gives two-way data binding on a form input?
questions.explication: `<input v-model="message">` updates `message` as the user types and updates the input when `message` changes. v-bind is one-way only.

questions.question: What is the shorthand for `v-on:click="handleClick"`?
questions.explication: `@` is the shorthand for v-on (events); `:` is the shorthand for v-bind (attributes).

questions.question: What is the shorthand for `v-bind:src="imageSource"`?
questions.explication: `:attr` = v-bind:attr. It binds an attribute dynamically to a data property.

questions.question:
Given `isVisible: false` and `isLoading: true`, what does this render? `
Visible content
` `
Loading...
` `
No data available
`
questions.explication: v-if is false, so Vue tests v-else-if, which is true: only "Loading..." is rendered.

questions.question: Why do we add `:key="item.id"` in `<li v-for="item in items" :key="item.id">`?
choix: To sort the list in ascending order using the id
To give each item a unique identity for updates
To make the items array editable with v-model
To display the id next to the item name
questions.explication: The key lets Vue track each element and update the list efficiently when items are added, removed or reordered.

questions.question: What are Vue.js directives?
choix: Special tokens in markup telling Vue to act on the DOM
CSS classes that Vue applies automatically
Global variables shared by every component in the app
Functions declared in the methods option
questions.explication: Directives (v-if, v-for, v-on, v-bind, v-model...) are special attributes in the template that tell Vue to do something to a DOM element.

questions.question: What are props used for in Vue components?
choix: Sending events from child to parent
Passing data from parent to child
questions.explication: `<my-component :message="parentMessage">` passes data down; the child declares `props: ['message']`.
questions.piege: Child → parent communication uses events (`$emit`), not props.

questions.question: How does a child component send data back to its parent?
questions.explication: The child emits a custom event with a payload; the parent listens with `@updateMessage="updateMessage"`.

questions.question: In Vue 3, to support `v-model` on a custom component, the component must...
choix: accept the `value` prop and emit the `input` event
use `v-bind` on its root element with `sync`
declare `v-model` as an entry inside its own `props` array
questions.explication: Vue 3 default: prop `modelValue` + event `update:modelValue`, e.g. `this.$emit('update:modelValue', event.target.value)`.

questions.question: In a child component template, what does `<slot></slot>` do?
choix: Shows content passed by the parent
Reserves space for an async component
Creates a new route for the component
Declares a prop received from the parent
questions.explication: Slots distribute content: whatever the parent places between `<my-component>...</my-component>` is rendered where `<slot>` is.

questions.question: How do you register a component globally in Vue 3?
questions.explication: In Vue 3 you call `app.component()` on the app returned by createApp. Vue 2 used `Vue.component()`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `const AsyncComponent = () => import('./AsyncComponent.vue');`?
choix: Render the component on the server side
Load the component only when needed
Fetch the component's data from an API
Run the component in a separate thread
questions.explication: Async components are lazy-loaded: the code is split and only downloaded when the component is needed, improving performance.

questions.question: In a Single File Component, what does `<style scoped>` do?
choix: Applies the styles to the whole application
Applies the styles to this component only
Converts the styles into inline style attributes
Loads the styles only after the page loads
questions.explication: An SFC (.vue) has three blocks: template, script, style. `scoped` limits the CSS to the current component.

questions.question:
`
A

Note

B
` gives a warning and "B" never behaves as expected. What is the bug?
choix: v-else must directly follow the v-if element
v-if cannot be used on a div element
The p element must also have v-if
v-else needs its own condition, like v-else="!ok"
questions.explication:
v-else (and v-else-if) must immediately follow an element with v-if or v-else-if. The `

` in between breaks the chain.

questions.question:
A Vue 3 component is written as `{ data: { count: 0 }, template: '

{{ count }}

' }` and fails. Why?
choix: The template must use v-text, not {{ }}
`count` must be declared inside the `computed` option
`data` must be a function returning an object
questions.explication: In components (and in Vue 3 apps) `data` must be a function: `data() { return { count: 0 }; }`, so each instance gets its own state.

questions.question: Clicking the button does nothing: `methods: { increment() { count += 1; } }`. What is the fix?
questions.explication: Inside methods, data properties are accessed through `this`. `count` alone is an undefined variable (ReferenceError).

questions.question: `<my-component message="parentMessage"></my-component>` displays the word "parentMessage" instead of its value. Why?
choix: The child must use `$emit` to read the value
The prop name must be written in capitals
questions.explication: Without `:`, the attribute is passed as a literal string. `:message="parentMessage"` evaluates the expression and passes the data value.

questions.question:
The child template uses `{{ message }}` and the parent passes `:message="msg"`, but nothing is shown. The child is `{ template: '
{{ message }}
' }`. What is missing?
questions.explication: The child must declare the props it receives (`props: ['message']`); otherwise `message` is not available in its template.

questions.question: What is the role of `<router-view>` in App.vue?
choix: It displays the component matching the current URL
It lists every route defined in the router
It creates a clickable link that navigates to another page
It reloads the page when the URL changes
questions.explication: `<router-view>` is the placeholder where Vue Router renders the component of the matched route.

questions.question: With the route `{ path: '/profile/:id', component: UserProfile }`, how does UserProfile read the id?
questions.explication: `$route` is the current route (params, query...); `$router` is the router object used to navigate.
questions.piege: `req.params.id` is the Express.js (server) equivalent, not Vue.

questions.question: How do you navigate to `/profile/123` from code in a Vue component?
questions.explication: `this.$router.push()` changes the route without reloading the page.

questions.question: Which statement describes Node.js?
choix: A template engine that uses indentation
A front-end framework for building reusable UI components
A database server for storing JSON data
A JavaScript runtime outside the browser, built on V8
questions.explication: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine. It is single-threaded, event-driven and non-blocking.

questions.question: What does `app.use(express.static('public'));` do?
choix: Sets 'public' as the folder where Pug views are stored
Makes every route in the app public (no auth)
Starts the server on the 'public' port
Serves files like CSS and images from 'public'
questions.explication: express.static is a middleware that serves static assets (images, CSS, JS) from the given folder.
questions.piege: The views folder is set with `app.set('views', './views')`.

questions.question:
Every request hangs after this middleware runs. What is wrong?
`app.use((req, res, next) => { console.log('Request at ' + Date.now()); });`
questions.explication: A middleware must either send a response or call `next()` to pass control on. Without it, the request-response cycle stops.

questions.question: In `app.post('/submit', (req, res) => res.send(req.body.username));`, `req.body` is undefined. What is the likely fix?
choix: Set Pug as the view engine for the app
questions.explication: Form data is only available in req.body after a body parser: `app.use(bodyParser.urlencoded({ extended: true }))` (or `express.urlencoded`).

questions.question: For the route `app.get('/user/:id', ...)`, how do you read the id in Express?
questions.explication: Route parameters are in `req.params`. Form data from POST is in `req.body`.

questions.question: How does Express recognise an error-handling middleware?
choix: It takes four arguments: (err, req, res, next)
It is always declared before every other route in the app
questions.explication: Express treats a middleware with 4 parameters `(err, req, res, next)` as an error handler, e.g. `res.status(500).send('Something went wrong!')`.

questions.question: With `- var name = "John"`, how do you display "Hello, John" in a paragraph?
questions.explication: Pug interpolates with `#{...}`. `{{ }}` is Vue syntax, `${}` is JS template literals, `<%= %>` is EJS.
questions.piege: `h1= message` (with =) outputs the whole value of a variable; `#{}` inserts it inside text.

questions.question: Which Pug code renders one `li` for each element of `items`?
choix: `ul` then indented `each item in items` / `li= item`
`ul` then indented `v-for item in items` / `li {{ item }}`
questions.explication: Pug loops with `each item in items`, and the indentation defines nesting. `li= item` outputs the value.

questions.question: `index.pug` starts with `extends layout`. What must it then define to fill the layout?
choix: A `mixin layout()` with exactly the same name
questions.explication: Template inheritance: layout.pug declares `block content`; index.pug uses `extends layout` and redefines `block content`.

questions.question: Given `mixin greeting(name)` / `p Hello #{name}`, how do you call the mixin?
questions.explication: Mixins are reusable blocks of markup (DRY). They are called with the `+` prefix.
